about: The cases every client runs against a real API (conformance/live/README.md). One list for all languages, so they run the same calls with the same params.

A param value "$name" is read from the fixture (discover.js writes it from the client's own data); "@caseId.field" is a field of the item an earlier case returned; "{client}" and "{run}" in a string are the client's name (node, python-sync, python-async, php) and the run's id.
A case whose fixture value is missing is skipped, never guessed.
class: read (GET), read-post (a POST that changes nothing, retried like a read), safe-write (changes nothing a client relies on: no funds move, nothing waits for an approval), negative, not-run.

paging: limit is the page size asked for, maxPages bounds how many pages are fetched, idField names each item (no item may come twice); everyItem compares the SDK's own iterator, at that page size, with one page of 50.

cases.why: The asset the address already holds, on that address: the API's 'already added' answer, which writes nothing.
A new deposit address on a test network; nothing moves and nothing waits for an approval.

A dry run of Create UTXO Transfer: the API creates nothing and reserves no UTXO. With no unspent UTXO in the vault the fixture names a spent one: an answer with sendersValid false, or a typed 4xx error, both pass.
No transaction request has this id: the answer must come back as a typed 4xx error, not a generic one.
A typed authentication error, sent once (never retried). Runs alone: no other call of this API key may be in flight (the gateway shares an in-flight key validation).

A client given response-signing roots is strict from its first answer: against an origin that does not sign (or a signature stripped from the start) the answer is refused as missing, sent once and never retried. The client gets the TEST-ONLY root of test-vectors/v1.json and an in-memory pin store, so the run's pin file is not touched.

Off unless VAULTODY_CONFORMANCE_BURST is set (README: on a small test environment a burst big enough for a 429 makes the API fail). That many reads from 4 workers (PHP: one after another), with the client's own limit lifted, then one deposit address in the same second: every read retried to success after a 429, the write run exactly once (one address with its label).
